column1: # THE BRIDGE. What this engine calls a colour token, and what it is called in
# the canonical design system.
# ⭐ NINE OF TEN WERE ONLY EVER A RENAME, and until that was written down the
# refit looked like a merge of two palettes. It is not. `surface` and `bg` are
# the same idea with two names, and the same is true eight more times.
# HOW IT IS USED. docrender/theme.py emits the CANONICAL name as the real
# declaration and this file as ALIASES after it:
#     --dr-text: #ecbd5b;
#     --dr-ink: var(--dr-text);
# So every `var(--dr-ink)` already written in a stylesheet keeps working, and
# nothing had to be found-and-replaced across the asset layer. New CSS should
# prefer the canonical name; the alias is a bridge, not a second vocabulary.
# A row where consumer == canonical emits NOTHING. An alias pointing a name at
# itself is a no-op in CSS and a trap in a table, because it reads as a mapping
# somebody chose.
# ⚠️ ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING WHERE THIS IS EMITTED, not here. The aliases must be
# written AFTER both the local base rows and the canonical block, or --dr-ink
# keeps the stand-in's value and the entire join silently does nothing while
# every file involved looks correct.
# Canonical record: mawizorek/maw-themes -> vocabulary/document-tokens.tsv,
# which carries the full reasoning per row plus the canonical roles this engine
# does not consume yet. This file is its projection, deliberately narrower: it
# holds only what the CSS emitter needs.
# consumer    the token name this engine's stylesheets already use
# canonical   the role name in the canonical system
# note        why, or what to watch
consumer
surface
surface-raised
column3: cards, admonition bodies, table zebra. Canonical splits raised chrome into surface-1/2/3; this engine has no top bar of its own (Material draws it), so what it calls raised is a PANEL, not chrome -- which is why this maps to 2 and not 1.
